children: Oil prices rose in early Asian trading Monday as renewed Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia heightened concerns about energy supplies and a broader Middle East conflict. The dollar also strengthened slightly as investors sought protection against geopolitical risks.

Saudi Arabia also is supporting a counteroffensive near Bab el-Mandeb, a strategic waterway connecting major shipping routes between Asia and Europe.

For investors, the latest attacks threaten to complicate an already challenging outlook for inflation, interest rates and corporate earnings. Prolonged oil prices above $100 a barrel could increase transportation and manufacturing costs, squeeze corporate profit margins and make it harder for central banks to contain inflation. Energy producers may benefit from higher crude prices, while airlines, transportation companies and other fuel-intensive businesses face additional pressure.

Markets are preparing for U.S. and European inflation reports this week, along with remarks from several central bank officials. Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh is scheduled to speak as traders assess the likelihood of further interest-rate increases. A stronger-than-expected September consumer price index could intensify pressure on Treasury bonds and reinforce expectations for tighter monetary policy.

Nick Twidale, chief market analyst at AT Global Markets in Sydney, warned that geopolitical developments could have an unusually large market impact, particularly with inflation figures, central bank speeches and the start of U.S. earnings season approaching.

U.S. stocks have remained resilient despite the turmoil. The S&P 500 reached a record high Tuesday before retreating on concerns about artificial intelligence demand. The index recovered Friday as investors anticipated another strong quarterly earnings season.

Analysts expect third-quarter earnings to increase approximately 25% from a year earlier, according to Bloomberg Intelligence, extending a streak of seven consecutive quarters of double-digit profit growth.
